title: Uniform Gieseker criterion from normalized codegree bounds
statement:
Fix integers $g\geq2$, $d\geq1$, $N\geq3$ and a real number $\epsilon>0$. There is an integer $M(g,d,N,\epsilon)$ with the following property over every algebraically closed field $k$ [def-weil-field]. Let $C$ be a smooth projective connected curve of genus $g=\dim_k H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ [def-sc-curves, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-kun-projective, def-pc-genus], let $L$ be an invertible module of degree $d$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-degree-line-bundle], and let $V\subset H^0(C,L)$ be an $N$-dimensional subspace whose evaluation defines a closed immersion $C\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(V^\vee)$. A full flag means $V=V_0\supset V_1\supset\cdots\supset V_{N-1}\supset0$ with $\dim_k V_i=N-i$. For each such flag put $A_i=\operatorname{im}(V_i\otimes_k\mathcal O_C\to L)$, an invertible submodule, and $e_i=d-\deg A_i$. For real weights $w_0\geq\cdots\geq w_{N-1}=0$ with $\sum_i w_i=1$ define
$$B(e,w)=\min_{0=i_0<\cdots<i_h=N-1}\sum_{j=0}^{h-1}(e_{i_j}+e_{i_{j+1}})(w_{i_j}-w_{i_{j+1}}).$$
Suppose that for every full flag and every such normalized weight tuple one has $B(e,w)\leq 2d/N-\epsilon$. Then for every $m\geq M(g,d,N,\epsilon)$ the Hilbert point of $C\subset\mathbf P(V^\vee)$, of Hilbert polynomial $P(m)=dm+1-g$, is stable for the natural $\operatorname{SL}(V)$ action and Hilbert determinant line $\Lambda_m$ of [lem-sfb-hilbert-plucker-pgl-linearization]. The bound is independent of $C,V,L,k$ and its characteristic. Stability has exactly the geometric meaning stated in that node; scheme conventions are [def-pc-scheme].

proof.text: The image modules $A_i$ in the statement are indeed invertible. For $0\leq i\leq N-1$ the subspace $V_i\subseteq H^0(C,L)$ is nonzero of dimension $N-i$, and $C$, $L$, $g\geq2$ satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-linear-series-degree-dimension-bound]. That node gives that $A_i=\operatorname{im}(V_i\otimes_k\mathcal O_C\to L)$ is an invertible submodule of $L$ generated by $V_i$, with $0\leq\deg A_i\leq d$. Each $v\in V_i$ is the image of $v\otimes1$, so $V_i\subseteq H^0(C,A_i)\subseteq H^0(C,L)$ and the evaluation map $V_i\otimes_k\mathcal O_C\to A_i$ is surjective. The original embedding says that $V$ generates $L$, so $A_0=L$; by the $q=1$ clause of the same node, $A_{N-1}\simeq\mathcal O_C$.

source.place: Morrison, Sections 2.2--2.3, Proposition 1, equations (3)--(5), Lemmas 2 and 4, printed pp.6--10; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0810.2340. Agent expansion of the omitted scalar calculation and of characteristic-independent uniformity by a fixed rounding mesh. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-product-subseries-eventual-fullness] with $p=0$ and $U=T=V$, $A=B=L$. For all sufficiently large $n$, restriction from $\operatorname{Sym}^n V$ is surjective and $h^0(C,L^{\otimes n})=dn+1-g$. Consequently the homogeneous-coordinate Hilbert polynomial is $P(t)=dt+1-g$. Put $K=2d/N-\epsilon$. Fix once and for all an integer $q>N$ with $q>4d/\epsilon$. By [lem-sfb-bounded-hilbert-weight-polynomials], with $(r,d,c,B)=(N,d,1-g,q)$, there are $m_0,A\geq1$ depending only on $N,g,d,q$, independent of the field and curve, such that for every compatible basis with integral weights $q\geq r_0\geq\cdots\geq r_{N-1}=0$ the minimum monomial-basis weight $W_r(m)$ satisfies $|W_r(m)-a_rm^2|\leq Am$ for $m\geq m_0$. Since all monomial weights are nonnegative, $a_r\geq0$ follows by dividing by $m^2$ and letting $m$ tend to infinity.

source.place: Morrison, Sections 2.2--2.3, Proposition 1, equations (3)--(5), Lemmas 2 and 4, printed pp.6--10; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0810.2340. Agent expansion of the omitted scalar calculation and of characteristic-independent uniformity by a fixed rounding mesh. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text:
Fix such an integral weighted flag, a subsequence $0=i_0<\cdots<i_h=N-1$, and $p\geq1$. Write $d_i=\deg A_i$ and $c=1-g$. For $0\leq j<h$, $0\leq l\leq p$, let $U_{j,l}^{(n)}$ be the image in $H^0(C,L^{\otimes n(p+1)})$ of the span of products of $n$ blocks, each block containing one factor from $V$, $p-l$ factors from $V_{i_j}$ and $l$ factors from $V_{i_{j+1}}$. Apply [lem-sfb-product-subseries-eventual-fullness] to $L,A_{i_j},A_{i_{j+1}}$ and their generating spaces. Its nonzero and generation hypotheses hold: each $V_i$ has dimension $N-i\geq1$ and generates $A_i$ by step 1 (the cited linear-series node), while $V$ generates $L$ and gives the assumed closed immersion. The spaces are viewed as subspaces of the sections of $A_i$ through $A_i\subseteq L$, as justified in step 1. Multiplication into $L^{\otimes(p+1)}$ and its powers is injective on the product invertible submodules: each inclusion $A_i\subseteq L$ stays injective after tensoring with invertible, hence flat, modules, and a composite of injections is injective. For all large $n$, therefore,
$$D_{j,l}:=\dim U_{j,l}^{(n)}=n\bigl(d+(p-l)d_{i_j}+l d_{i_{j+1}}\bigr)+c.$$
Only finitely many pairs $(j,l)$ are involved, so one $n_0$ works for this fixed $p$, flag and curve. No uniformity in this $n_0$ will be used.

source.place: Morrison, Sections 2.2--2.3, Proposition 1, equations (3)--(5), Lemmas 2 and 4, printed pp.6--10; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0810.2340. Agent expansion of the omitted scalar calculation and of characteristic-independent uniformity by a fixed rounding mesh. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text:
The spaces just defined form a decreasing chain as $l$ increases, with $U_{j,p}^{(n)}=U_{j+1,0}^{(n)}$. Since $i_0=0$ and $V_0=V$, every degree-$n(p+1)$ coordinate monomial can be partitioned into $n$ blocks of $p+1$ factors, so the initial space is exactly the image of $\operatorname{Sym}^{n(p+1)}V$. Step 2 makes this all of $H^0(C,L^{\otimes n(p+1)})$ for large $n$. Each space is spanned by degree-$n(p+1)$ monomials of weight at most
$$t_{j,l}=n\bigl(r_0+(p-l)r_{i_j}+lr_{i_{j+1}}\bigr).$$
Here one factor from $V$ has weight at most $r_0$, and each factor from $V_i$ at most $r_i$, by the compatible basis. Starting from a monomial basis of the last space, extend backwards to a monomial basis of each preceding space; a spanning set contains a basis extension. Its total weight is at most the sum of $(D_{j,l-1}-D_{j,l})t_{j,l-1}$ over successive drops plus the final dimension times its cap. Telescoping, and using the formula for $D_{j,l}$, gives
$$W_r(n(p+1))\leq\bigl(n(p+1)d+c\bigr)n(p+1)r_0+\sum_{j=0}^{h-1}\sum_{l=1}^p D_{j,l}\,n(r_{i_{j+1}}-r_{i_j}).$$
Repeated spaces and repeated weights cause zero drops and do not change this identity.

source.place: Morrison, Sections 2.2--2.3, Proposition 1, equations (3)--(5), Lemmas 2 and 4, printed pp.6--10; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0810.2340. Agent expansion of the omitted scalar calculation and of characteristic-independent uniformity by a fixed rounding mesh. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text:
Divide the preceding inequality by $n^2(p+1)^2$ and let $n\to\infty$. The error estimate in step 2 identifies the left limit with $a_r$; the terms containing $c/n$ vanish. Since $\sum_{l=1}^p l=p(p+1)/2$ and $\sum_{l=1}^p(p-l)=p(p-1)/2$, the result is
$$a_r\leq dr_0+\frac{p}{(p+1)^2}\sum_{j=0}^{h-1}(r_{i_{j+1}}-r_{i_j})\left(d+\frac{p-1}{2}d_{i_j}+\frac{p+1}{2}d_{i_{j+1}}\right).$$
This holds for every positive integer $p$. Letting $p\to\infty$ now yields
$$2a_r\leq 2dr_0+\sum_{j=0}^{h-1}(d_{i_j}+d_{i_{j+1}})(r_{i_{j+1}}-r_{i_j})=\sum_{j=0}^{h-1}(e_{i_j}+e_{i_{j+1}})(r_{i_j}-r_{i_{j+1}}).$$
For the equality substitute $d_i=d-e_i$ and telescope $\sum_j(r_{i_j}-r_{i_{j+1}})=r_0$ since $r_{N-1}=0$. Taking the minimum over the finite set of subsequences gives $2a_r\leq B(e,r)$, where the same displayed definition of $B$ is used without normalizing $r$.

source.place: Morrison, Sections 2.2--2.3, Proposition 1, equations (3)--(5), Lemmas 2 and 4, printed pp.6--10; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0810.2340. Agent expansion of the omitted scalar calculation and of characteristic-independent uniformity by a fixed rounding mesh. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text:
For any ordered basis and any rational tuple $w_0\geq\cdots\geq w_{N-1}=0$, $\sum_iw_i=1$, put $r_i=\lfloor qw_i\rfloor$ and $R=\sum_i r_i$. These are ordered integers in $[0,q]$ with last entry zero and $q-N<R\leq q$, hence $R>0$. The tuple $r/R$ is normalized and belongs to the same full flag. For each subsequence, its defining sum at $r$ is $R$ times its sum at $r/R$. Since $R>0$, taking the minimum preserves this factor; the hypothesis gives $B(e,r)=R B(e,r/R)\leq RK$. Step 5 gives $0\leq2a_r\leq RK$, so $K\geq0$ for any curve satisfying the hypothesis, and $a_r/q\leq K/2$ since $R\leq q$. Choose a monomial basis minimizing $W_r(m)$. Each degree-$m$ monomial has $w$-weight at most its $r$-weight divided by $q$ plus $m/q$, because $0\leq w_i-r_i/q<1/q$. There are $P(m)$ monomials in that basis. Thus for $m\geq m_0$,
$$W_w(m)\leq W_r(m)/q+mP(m)/q\leq (d/N-\epsilon/2)m^2+(A/q)m+mP(m)/q.$$
This is a comparison of the same finite sets of monomials, so it requires no continuity theorem for Hilbert weights.

source.place: Morrison, Sections 2.2--2.3, Proposition 1, equations (3)--(5), Lemmas 2 and 4, printed pp.6--10; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0810.2340. Agent expansion of the omitted scalar calculation and of characteristic-independent uniformity by a fixed rounding mesh. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text:
Enlarge $M$ to be at least $m_0$, $1$, and the field-independent Hilbert-embedding threshold of [lem-sfb-hilbert-plucker-pgl-linearization], and choose it strictly larger than $4\bigl(A/q+(g-1)/N\bigr)/\epsilon$. Since $g\geq2$, $P(m)\leq dm$. Step 6 and $q>4d/\epsilon$ therefore give, for every normalized rational weighted basis and all $m\geq M$,
$$W_w(m)-mP(m)/N\leq(-\epsilon/2+d/q)m^2+\bigl(A/q+(g-1)/N\bigr)m<0.$$
All constants depend only on $g,d,N,\epsilon$.

source.place: Morrison, Sections 2.2--2.3, Proposition 1, equations (3)--(5), Lemmas 2 and 4, printed pp.6--10; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0810.2340. Agent expansion of the omitted scalar calculation and of characteristic-independent uniformity by a fixed rounding mesh. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text:
Given any ordered basis and nonconstant rational weights $u_i$, reorder the basis to make them decreasing, put $a=\min_i u_i$, $S=\sum_i(u_i-a)>0$, and $w_i=(u_i-a)/S$. This is one of the full flags and normalized tuples already tested. Every degree-$m$ monomial-basis weight transforms by $W_u(m)=S W_w(m)+amP(m)$, while $\sum_i u_i=S+Na$. Consequently
$$W_u(m)-\frac{\sum_i u_i}{N}mP(m)=S\bigl(W_w(m)-mP(m)/N\bigr)<0.$$
Apply [lem-sfb-hilbert-monomial-numerical-criterion] to obtain stability of the Hilbert point for $\operatorname{SL}(V)$ and $\Lambda_m$, with the geometric stability convention of [lem-sfb-hilbert-plucker-pgl-linearization]. The product-series input was pointwise over arbitrary algebraically closed fields, and the only uniform geometric estimate was [lem-sfb-bounded-hilbert-weight-polynomials], whose constants are independent of characteristic. Hence this single $M$ works over every such field.
